clue.text: Beauty parlour mainly discussed darling's outfit for Chamonix?

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a beauty parlour is a salon

indicators.note: discussed means spoken about, so we want a word sounding like the one said

parts.note: a darling is a pet, plus the 's, giving PETS

explanation.surface: Someone describes, in a roundabout way, what a beloved pet from the beauty salon wore at a ski resort.
explanation.walkthrough: SALON loses its last letter to give SALO; PETTES is said the same as PETS. Chamonix is a French Alpine ski resort, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Salopettes are padded ski trousers with a bib and braces, the typical clothing on the slopes at a ski resort.

clue.text: Sweltering before temperature dropped somewhere in New York

indicators.note: dropped means the named letter is let fall out of the word

parts.note: sweltering means so hot

explanation.surface: A weather report: a heatwave came before the thermometer fell somewhere in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: SoHo is a district of Lower Manhattan, as well as of London.
explanation.definitionFit: SoHo is a neighbourhood in Manhattan, short for South of Houston Street, so it is a place within the city.

clue.text: Vacant latrine flushed after pee — it's a condition

indicators.note: after places the flushed word behind the letter P
vacant means emptied, so only the outside letters of the word stay

parts.note: pee is the spelt-out name of the letter P
flushed means red in the face, rosy

explanation.surface: A toilet scene: an empty latrine gets flushed after someone pees, and that's a medical condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flushed' and 'pee' play up the toilet picture, but they are rosy and the letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: Leprosy is a chronic bacterial disease, a medical condition affecting skin and nerves.

clue.text: Perhaps Peter, since new housing scam, fearful

parts.note: Peter Pan, the boy who never grew up, is an example of a Pan

indicators.note: housing means holding another word inside
new means the letters are made afresh in a different order

parts.note: a scam is a trick

explanation.surface: Someone called Peter becomes frightened because a new scheme is housing a scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps Peter' points to the fictional Peter Pan rather than any real Peter; the rearranged 'since' wraps around the scam word.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic-stricken describes being overcome by sudden fear, an intense form of fearful.

clue.text: Greek astronomer Ptolemy ultimately finding ideal situation

parts.note: Theo is a Greek first name (short for Theodore, from theos, god)

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: The Greek astronomer Ptolemy eventually discovers a perfect place in the cosmos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek astronomer Ptolemy' reads as one man, but 'Greek' is the name THEO and 'ultimately' takes R and Y from the ends of the other two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that work 'in theory' work in an idealised scenario, so theory is the ideal as opposed to practice.

clue.text: Itinerant rep's in good company if wanting to top up drink

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the company name

parts.words: good company if wanting to top up
parts.note: Esso is a petrol company, a good place to go if you need to top up your tank

indicators.note: itinerant means wandering about, so these letters roam into a new order

parts.note: the letters of rep plus the s of 's

explanation.surface: A travelling sales rep is in good company if they want to top up their drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top up' sounds like refilling a glass, but it means filling a car with petrol at a forecourt.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is a strong coffee forced through ground beans under pressure, a type of drink.

clue.text: Regulars inside getting at smoker?

indicators.note: regular letters from inside the phrase, taking every second one

explanation.surface: A dig at a smoker, with the regulars indoors getting at them.
explanation.walkthrough: Every second letter of GETTING AT gives E, T, N, A. Etna smokes as an active volcano, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is an active Sicilian volcano that regularly emits plumes of smoke and ash.

clue.text: Pair at bridge entering characteristic passage

indicators.note: entering means going into the other word

parts.note: a characteristic is a trait
in the card game bridge North and South are partners, a pair

explanation.surface: Two people at a bridge enter a passage typical of the place.
explanation.walkthrough: North and South form a partnership at bridge, giving NS.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit means passage or the act of passing through or across somewhere.

clue.text: Like attending sport, excited to see F1 driver earlier

parts.note: a la, as in the style of, means like
attending means being in, present

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic fan attends motor sport, excited to see a racing driver arrive early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earlier' makes the definition a former driver rather than a current one.
explanation.definitionFit: Alain Prost is a French four-time Formula One world champion from the 1980s and 1990s, now retired.

clue.text: Each vagrant clutching pound coin, as it were

indicators.note: clutching means holding the next word inside
vagrant means wandering, so the letters stray into a new order

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, a pen

explanation.surface: A homeless person each time clutches a pound coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money beside 'coin', but it is an animal enclosure. 'as it were' covers ha'pence being an amount rather than one coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Ha'pence is the old British halfpenny sum, money in small change, roughly a coin value.

clue.text: VW, a banger perhaps coated in this red stuff?

definitions.text: banger perhaps coated in this red stuff?

parts.note: the Passat is a Volkswagen car model

explanation.surface: A clapped-out Volkswagen, a banger, has been painted red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banger' suggests an old car next to the VW, but here it is a sausage, which might be cooked in tomato sauce. A banger is British slang for both.
explanation.definitionFit: Passata is sieved uncooked tomato purée, a red sauce that a sausage might be served in.

clue.text: Female Aussie comedian no longer an actress

parts.note: sheila is Australian slang for a woman
Tony Hancock was a British comedian who died in 1968

explanation.surface: A female Australian comic has given up comedy for acting.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheila Hancock is a well-known English stage and screen performer, star of Inspector Morse spin-offs and West End shows.

clue.text: Jazzman, tense during openers, played with gong

parts.note: a gong is slang for an award, such as an Oscar

indicators.note: during means placed inside the other word
played means performed in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A jazz musician, tense in his opening numbers, is accompanied by a gong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with gong' comes last in the clue, but the award leads the answer; the tense letter joins the opening numbers before they are played into the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Peterson was a celebrated Canadian jazz pianist, one of the great musicians of the genre.

clue.text: On yacht without husband? It's a riotous holiday

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters are thrown into a new order
without means minus the named letter

parts.note: the letters of it's without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Aboard a yacht with no husband, the holiday becomes a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking H from ON YACHT leaves ONYACT; with ITS and A, 'riotous' rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A staycation is a vacation spent at home or in one's own country rather than travelling abroad.

clue.text: Apply horn around variable area for road user

indicators.note: around means wrapping the other letter

parts.note: to apply a horn is to toot
Y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A driver is told to sound the horn round a stretch of road.
explanation.walkthrough: TOOT goes around Y to make TOYOT, and A for area follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A Toyota is a Japanese car, a vehicle that travels on roads.

clue.text: Recluse is panning a lot in presence of gold

indicators.note: panning, as in washing gravel for gold, swirls these letters into a new order

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A hermit spends a lot of time panning for gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'panning' fits the gold-prospecting picture but stirs A LOT into OLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An isolator is one who keeps apart from others, as a hermit or loner does.

clue.text: Old music producer's hand on deck during record, spinning tracks

indicators.note: during means sitting within the other word
spinning means turning round, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
a deckhand is a sailor, an old salt
RY is the abbreviation for railway, tracks

explanation.surface: An old music producer's deckhand is spinning tracks during a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old music producer' sounds like a record-company veteran, but it is an antique instrument; 'tracks' are railway lines, not songs.
explanation.definitionFit: A psaltery is an ancient stringed instrument plucked with the fingers, a source of music.

clue.text: Unknown, inclined to eat pastries, extremely gassy

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown

indicators.note: to eat means to take the other word inside

parts.note: inclined, as in apt to do something, means apt
pies are pastries

explanation.surface: Someone unknown, given to eating pastries, becomes very windy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gassy' looks like flatulence, but it means chattering.
explanation.definitionFit: Gassy can mean talkative, and yappy is chattering noisily, so the superlative is most talkative.

clue.text: Group drafting draw, just one time, in felt-tip?

indicators.note: in means placed inside the pen

parts.note: a felt-tip is a pen

indicators.note: just one time means keeping only one of the two Ts

parts.note: a lotto is a lottery draw

explanation.surface: A sketcher drafts a picture once with a felt-tip pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drafting' suggests drawing with the felt-tip, but it means riding in another's slipstream.
explanation.definitionFit: A peloton is the main bunch of riders in a cycle race, who ride in each other's slipstream to save energy.

clue.text: Help thugs filling out hit lists?

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady, domestic help

indicators.note: with the filling out, only the outer letters of the word stay

explanation.surface: A domestic helper is filling out the gang's lists of people to rub out.
explanation.walkthrough: A char, or charwoman, is British for a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: The charts rank the best-selling music, so they are lists of hit records.

clue.text: Test might be concerned with reserve of old knowledge

parts.note: re means about, concerned with
TA was the Territorial Army, the old name for the British Army Reserve
ken means range of knowledge

explanation.surface: An exam on old reservists' knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA was renamed the Army Reserve in 2014, hence 'of old'.
explanation.definitionFit: A failed exam may be sat again, so retaken is what a test might end up being.

clue.text: Religious doctrine's final word about spiritual books

indicators.note: about means going around the other letters

parts.note: ta-ra is a northern English goodbye, a last word
NT is the New Testament, a set of sacred books

explanation.surface: A religious teaching's last word is about holy books.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantra is a body of Hindu and Buddhist esoteric teaching, a system of religious belief.

clue.text: Probably lost key, alas, in rubbish

indicators.note: rubbish means poorly done, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone probably lost their key in the bin, alas.
explanation.definitionFit: As likely as not is an idiom for an even or better chance, roughly meaning probably.

clue.text: Complaint line is out of hand

indicators.note: is out of means the letter leaves the word

parts.note: a hand is a style of handwriting

explanation.surface: A grievance about a queue that has got out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand' here is handwriting, a style.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a minor medical ailment.

clue.text: Concentrated energy concluding how cash may be dispensed

indicators.note: concluding means coming at the end of the answer

parts.note: a cash machine may give out notes in tens
E is the physics abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: Focused effort ends with how an ATM gives out money.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense can mean strong and undiluted, the same sense as a concentrated flavour.

clue.text: Flier taking odd look inside where plane's stored?

indicators.note: taking, with inside, means the bird holds the other letters
inside completes the containment signal

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, a flier

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An airman takes a curious peek inside the hangar where his aircraft is kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' and 'plane' suggest aviation, but the flier is a small bird and the plane is a woodworking tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A toolkit is a set of tools, where a carpenter's plane for smoothing wood would be kept.

clue.text: Section of Matterhorn on own? Impossible

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Climbing part of the Matterhorn alone is out of the question.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-no is something not allowed or out of the question, so it is impossible to do.

clue.text: Suspiciously observe Yankee with aces under the table

indicators.note: under the table means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A card cheat from America hides aces under the table, so watch him warily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under the table' suggests hiding cards, but it means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye askance is to look at something with distrust or disapproval, a sidelong look.
